# pbs_traffic_control_rule (Resource)

Manages a Proxmox Backup Server traffic control rule: a bandwidth limit on the connections clients from some networks open to PBS on its port, 8007 — backups, restores, and the sync jobs of other servers — optionally only for some users, or at some times. `rate_in` limits what PBS receives, such as backups, and `rate_out` what it sends, such as restores. All the connections a rule applies to share its limits.

**One rule per connection.** PBS applies the one rule that matches a connection best: of the rules whose `network`, `users` and `timeframe` match, a rule with `users` beats one without, and then the one with the longest matching network prefix wins; between equals, PBS picks either. A direction the winning rule sets no rate for is not limited, so a rule without rates exempts its clients from a broader one. PBS documents that all matching rules apply, but its code picks one.

Connections PBS opens itself are not limited by these rules: sync jobs and S3 endpoints have rate limits of their own. PBS applies a change to open connections within seconds. Time frames are in the server's local time.

Managing traffic control rules needs `Sys.Modify on /`; reading them `Sys.Audit on /`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# On working days from 8:00 to 18:00, server time, the clients in the office
# network share 100 MB per second for what they send PBS, such as backups,
# and 50 MB per second for what PBS sends them, such as restores, so that
# backups leave bandwidth for the office. At other times the rule does not
# apply, and nothing is limited. Only connections clients open to PBS are
# limited: sync jobs and S3 endpoints have rate limits of their own.
resource "pbs_traffic_control_rule" "office" {
  name      = "office"
  network   = ["192.0.2.0/24", "2001:db8:1::/48"]
  timeframe = ["mon..fri 8:00-18:00"]
  rate_in   = "100MB"
  rate_out  = "50MB"
  comment   = "Office hours"
}

# PBS applies one rule to a connection, the best match, and a rule with users
# beats one without. So another PBS that pulls from this one as offsite@pbs
# gets 20 MB per second from any network, office included, at any time
# (PBS 4.1+). After a quiet period, up to 200 MB pass at once.
resource "pbs_traffic_control_rule" "offsite_pulls" {
  name      = "offsite-pulls"
  network   = ["0.0.0.0/0", "::/0"]
  users     = ["offsite@pbs"]
  rate_out  = "20MB"
  burst_out = "200MB"
  comment   = "Pulls of pbs-offsite.example.com"
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Rule name, 3 to 32 characters: letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`, not starting with `.` or `-`. Changing it replaces the rule.
- `network` (Set of String) Client networks the rule applies to, in CIDR notation, such as `192.0.2.0/24` or `2001:db8::/32`; `0.0.0.0/0` and `::/0` together for every client, as a rule for some `users` needs.

### Optional

- `burst_in` (String) How many bytes over `rate_in` PBS may receive at once, after a quiet period; as much as `rate_in` when left out. Requires `rate_in`. A byte size such as `500`, `64KiB`, `10MiB` or `1.5GB`: `K`, `M`, `G`, `T` and `P` are powers of 1000, `Ki` to `Pi` powers of 1024, and `B` is optional. PBS writes it back in its own spelling, such as `10 MiB`, which counts as the same: state keeps the configuration's. Only after an import, state has PBS's spelling, and the next plan shows an update that sends nothing.
- `burst_out` (String) How many bytes over `rate_out` PBS may send at once, after a quiet period; as much as `rate_out` when left out. Requires `rate_out`. A byte size such as `500`, `64KiB`, `10MiB` or `1.5GB`: `K`, `M`, `G`, `T` and `P` are powers of 1000, `Ki` to `Pi` powers of 1024, and `B` is optional. PBS writes it back in its own spelling, such as `10 MiB`, which counts as the same: state keeps the configuration's. Only after an import, state has PBS's spelling, and the next plan shows an update that sends nothing.
- `comment` (String) Free-form comment, up to 128 characters on one line.
- `rate_in` (String) Rate limit on the data PBS receives from the matching clients together, such as backups, in bytes per second; no limit when left out. A byte size such as `500`, `64KiB`, `10MiB` or `1.5GB`: `K`, `M`, `G`, `T` and `P` are powers of 1000, `Ki` to `Pi` powers of 1024, and `B` is optional. PBS writes it back in its own spelling, such as `10 MiB`, which counts as the same: state keeps the configuration's. Only after an import, state has PBS's spelling, and the next plan shows an update that sends nothing.
- `rate_out` (String) Rate limit on the data PBS sends to the matching clients together, such as restores, in bytes per second; no limit when left out. A byte size such as `500`, `64KiB`, `10MiB` or `1.5GB`: `K`, `M`, `G`, `T` and `P` are powers of 1000, `Ki` to `Pi` powers of 1024, and `B` is optional. PBS writes it back in its own spelling, such as `10 MiB`, which counts as the same: state keeps the configuration's. Only after an import, state has PBS's spelling, and the next plan shows an update that sends nothing.
- `timeframe` (Set of String) Times the rule applies at, each a time range with optional days, such as `8-17`, `mon..fri 8:00-18:00` or `sat,sun 10:00-14:30`, in the server's local time; always when left out. A range includes its start but not its end, and cannot cross midnight: `22-24` is refused, `22:00-23:59` ends a minute early.
- `users` (Set of String) Users the rule applies to, such as `sync@pbs`, from the matching networks; connections of an API token count as its user's, and connections that have not signed in as none. Every client when left out. Needs PBS 4.1 or newer.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same value as `name`, present because Terraform requires an `id`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_traffic_control_rule.office
  identity = {
    name = "office"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `name` (String) Rule name, such as `office`.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_traffic_control_rule.office
  id = "office"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Traffic control rules are imported by name, as Configuration → Traffic
# Control in the web interface, or the pbs_traffic_control_rules data source,
# shows it.
terraform import pbs_traffic_control_rule.office office
```
